exposure: type of attempted uterine incision (low transverse vs. classical)
outcome: Composite maternal outcome (postpartum hemorrhage, transfusion, endometritis, sepsis, wound infection, deep venous thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, hysterectomy, respiratory complications, and intensive care unit admission)
cohort: Women undergoing cesarean delivery between 23 0/7 and 27 6/7 weeks' gestation from 2005 through 2014
finding: Attempting a low transverse uterine incision compared to a classical incision in very preterm cesarean deliveries was associated with similar odds of composite maternal outcome but shorter operative time, while the conversion rate from low transverse to inverted T incision was low.
